city_center.notes: El Paso means 'the pass of the north' -- the Rio Grande gap between the Franklin Mountains and the mountains of Juarez. Ysleta and Socorro missions (1680s) anchor the lower valley. sources: Franklin Mountains geography (beg.utexas.edu); El Paso Missions (texasbeyondhistory.net); Adobe in West Texas (preservationtexas.org).

cultural_notes: El Paso means 'the pass of the north' (originally El Paso del Norte) -- the Rio Grande gap between the Franklin Mountains and the mountains south of the border (source: beg.utexas.edu Texas Through Time, Franklin Mountains)

the region holds 350-year-old adobe structures; Spanish missionaries built adobe churches and missions at Ysleta and Socorro in the 1680s, and those missions shaped nearby residential adobe (source: Adobe in West Texas, preservationtexas.org; A guide to El Paso's architectural history, elpasomatters.org)

the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo (Tigua) is the surviving Native community that has maintained cultural identity through the mission era -- any tribal reference stays consent-gated (source: El Paso Missions, texasbeyondhistory.net)

Chihuahuita and El Segundo Barrio are the historic border neighborhoods where El Paso's urbanization began -- deeply Mexican-American, muralist, migrant-farmworker heritage (source: savingplaces.org 2016 endangered list)
